subject: Lumena Health: custom SLA addendum, order form language and DocuSign timeline
messages:
From: Sara D'Souza <sara@lumenahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenahealth.com, Lumena Legal <legal@lumenahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum and order form language for Lumena MSA

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. We had a quick procurement sync this morning and two asks came up that are blockers for our security & procurement teams before we can sign the MSA + order form:

1) Uptime: Lumena requires a written addendum to the MSA with a 99.95% monthly uptime commitment and a defined credit schedule for availability breaches.

2) Latency: Our product team needs a p95 / p99 guidance for the inference endpoints used in our clinical routing flow (we need p99 <= 300ms for text-generation embeddings in the US region under normal traffic). If you cannot commit to p99, we need fallback and routing guarantees documented (how requests degrade, how fallbacks to a smaller model affect cost/latency).

Separately, we are collecting evidence: SOC2 report and 30 days of uptime/latency logs for a similar customer profile would speed legal signoff. Can Redwood provide an evidence packet and a proposed order form clause we can show our legal team?

Can you also share a DocuSign timeline? Our Q3 onboarding kickoff is scheduled the week of 2028-07-11, so ideally we’d have signed docs by 2028-06-30.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if helpful.

Best,
Sara D'Souza
Senior Program Manager, Vendor Operations
Lumena Health

Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum and order form language for Lumena MSA

Sara —

Really appreciate the clarity. I’ve attached an initial draft SLA addendum and an annotated order form snippet for the latency language (RDW-SLA-Addendum-draft-1.pdf; OrderForm-Lumena-draft.docx). High-level responses:

- Uptime: We can offer a 99.95% monthly availability objective for the Hosted API in the primary US region subject to the exceptions below and a standard credit schedule. I included the proposed credit table in the attached draft.

- Latency: For the inference endpoints you mentioned, we can commit to a p95 SLA at 200ms and a p99 objective (best-effort) at 300ms for production traffic on our curated model build. We do not currently guarantee p99 latency under sustained overloaded tail conditions; the addendum includes fallback routing rules and a defined degraded-mode behavior (automatic model-variant fallback plus call-level caching).

- Evidence: We can compile a packet: SOC 2 Type II summary, a redacted 30-day uptime/latency export for a comparable tenant, and a short ops runbook that maps notification flows. I flagged the artifacts in the attachments.

Next steps I propose:
1) Lumena confirms any non-standard signers and the procurement timeline.
2) Our Legal (cc'd) and Contracts teams review the draft addendum and provide redlines by EOD Mon (2028-06-18).
3) I’ll circulate a final-ready PDF and a DocuSign envelope link once legal redlines are resolved; target sign-by 2028-06-30 to meet your onboarding date.

If you want to tighten the p99 guarantee, we can discuss a dedicated-capacity commitment (Dedicated pool) — that’s an additional commercial path but gives stronger latency SLOs. Happy to outline the cost delta.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Lumena Health: custom SLA addendum — redlines and evidence scope

Marcus —

Quick notes after a first pass through RDW-SLA-Addendum-draft-1.pdf:

1) Credit cap: We should keep a monthly cap equal to 3x the monthly service fees or a pro rata monthly cap rather than uncapped language. I added a table in the attached redline (SLA-addendum-redline-karthik.docx).

2) Force majeure / maintenance carveout: Expand the scheduled maintenance window language and add a notification SLA (24 hours for planned maintenance >30 minutes).

3) Evidence and audit rights: Lumena asked for a 30-day export. Ops can provide a redacted 30-day performance export and a summary SOC2 statement; however, full audit rights or raw log exports need stricter gating. Propose a packaged evidence handoff: SOC2 summary + 30-day aggregated uptime/latency CSV + sanitized example traces. We should require an NDA addendum for any raw logs.

4) Latency guarantees: I agree with the p95 guarantee and p99 objective. For legal I suggest labeling p99 as an "operational objective" rather than a contractual SLA to avoid credit triggers for tail conditions. If Lumena insists on contractual p99 we should move to Dedicated or explicitly tie it to burst protection commitments.

5) Fallbacks & rollback: Add a clause that describes automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and the expected functional delta (token cost change, possible reranking variance).

If you want I can draft a redline markup to return to Lumena Legal. Naomi — please confirm the evidence package lead time so I can include it in our reply.

- Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Sara / Lumena team —

Thanks for your patience. Per our internal review we’ve finalized the SLA addendum and the order form language. Changes since the draft: Karthik tightened the credit cap and maintenance carveouts, Naomi confirmed evidence packaging and collection lead times. Attachments: RDW-SLA-Addendum-final.pdf (final addendum), OrderForm-Lumena-draft.docx (order form snippet).

Key points and next steps:
- Availability: 99.95% monthly availability objective for the Hosted API (primary US region). Credit schedule is in section 3 of the addendum; monthly credit cap equals 3x monthly service fees.
- Latency: p95 contractual SLA at 200ms, p99 operational objective at 300ms. p99 remains an objective (non-credit-bearing) unless Lumena elects a Dedicated capacity path — we can include pricing if you want firm p99 contractual guarantees.
- Evidence handoff: Ops will provide SOC2 summary + redacted 30-day aggregated uptime/latency CSV + sanitized trace examples. Naomi confirms we can deliver this bundle within 3 business days after countersignature. Raw logs will require an NDA addendum.
- Fallback behavior: Documented automatic model-variant fallback and degraded-mode behavior; functional tradeoffs described in appendix A.

DocuSign: I’ve created an envelope for the final PDF. Please review and sign by 2028-06-30 so we can meet your July onboarding kickoff. DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e

If Lumena Legal wants any additional tweaks I can accept minor redlines in DocuSign comments; major changes will require a second countersign round.

Would you like a 20-minute call Monday to walk through section 3 (credits) and the evidence package? I’m available 09:00–12:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to getting you onboarded.

Marcus Lin
Senior Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
